# @chi-hong22/dsh-plan-spend

A usage popup for the DSH Web GUI: the "Usage" sidebar navigation row opens a
panel showing the plan
spend of the **configured** providers.
## What it shows
| Provider | Source | Rendered |
| DeepSeek official | the DeepSeek **account sign-in**: the host half asks `ctx.deepseekAccount.reso
lveToken` for the grant and calls `GET https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance` with `x-dsh-auth-token
`; falls back to the same endpoint with `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` | recharge balance (server precision kept
), the topped-up split on the fallback card, the bonus wallet when the account holds one, the suffic
iency flag, which route the number came from, and the **peak / off-peak** window with its next switc

h |
| OpenCode Go | `GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage` | 5-hour / 7-day / monthly used percen
tage, progress bar, reset countdown |

**赠金 (granted credit) gets its own row.** It is promotional and short-lived,
so it is not plan balan

ce and does not count towards the recharge balance: when
the account actually holds some, the card a

dds a 赠金 line under the recharge
balance and hides it again at zero. Both routes map `granted_balanc

e`; the
account card's headline figure still comes from `topped_up_balance` alone.

**Known limitation**: the OpenCode Go usage endpoint returns percentages and
reset instants only — n

o used/limit amounts. That column is therefore
percent-only; the exact dollar figures live in the Op

ounts. That column is therefore
percent-only; the exact dollar figures live in the OpenCode console.
## Peak and off-peak (DeepSeek official)

DeepSeek bills two rates, and off-peak is half the peak price, so the DeepSeek
card carries one more

row: whether the current moment is peak or off-peak, and
how long until the next switch.

There is **no endpoint** that reports the current window — the rule lives in a
footnote on the prici

ng page — so this row derives it client-side from the
published rule:

- **Peak**: Monday–Friday `09:00–12:00` and `14:00–18:00` Beijing time (UTC
`01:00–04:00` and `06:00

–10:00`), **excluding Chinese public holidays**.
- **Everything else is off-peak**: `12:00–14:00`, t

he night, **all weekend**, and
**public holidays in full**.
How the derivation is pinned down:

- **Weekends are always off-peak**, so a make-up workday that lands on a Saturday
or Sunday needs no

extra modelling — the weekend rule already calls it off-peak.
- The holiday set is therefore the **

whole published State Council arrangement**
(including workdays folded into a holiday, such as 2 Jan

uary for New Year), not
just the 11 statutory days; otherwise peak would reappear mid-holiday.
- Loo

kups use **UTC date keys**: every peak window lies inside UTC `00:00–16:00`
and everything outside a

window is off-peak, so a UTC-date lookup and a
Beijing-date lookup agree.
- The windows are **half-
open**: `04:00:00` sharp is already off-peak.
### The holiday table needs upkeep

The table is `UM_CHINA_PUBLIC_HOLIDAYS_UTC` in `client.body.js` (33 days for
2026, from State Counci

l notice 国办发明电〔2025〕7 号); the years it covers are
listed in `UM_HOLIDAY_YEARS`. Each **fourth quarte

r**, once the State Council
publishes the next year's arrangement, append that year's date keys and

ate Council
publishes the next year's arrangement, append that year's date keys and the year
itself.

When the table does not cover the current year the card says so outright — the
holiday table does no

t cover that year, add the data — because in that state
every weekday statutory holiday would be sco

red as peak, and **a wrong number
stated silently is worse than a missing one declared**. A covered

year shows no
notice at all.

## Configuration

The plugin has no config. It decides which providers to show from whether their
credential is config

ured; the reference names live in the `ADAPTERS` table in
`index.js`:
| Provider | Credential ref (POSIX environment name) |

| DeepSeek official | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` |
| OpenCode Go | `OPENCODEGO_API_KEY` |

Credentials resolve through `ctx.credentials.resolve()`; the source precedence
is documented by `@de

epseek-ai/dsh-credentials-local` (launch environment →
stored file → project `.env` → harness home `

.env`). **An unconfigured provider
issues no request** and renders as "no credential configured; ski

. **An unconfigured provider
issues no request** and renders as "no credential configured; skipped".

The API-key row is the **fallback**. The DeepSeek card is normally read in this
half from the signed

-in DeepSeek account: `ctx.deepseekAccount.resolveToken`
hands out the stored grant for the configur

ed inference origin
(`https://api.deepseek.com`), and that token goes to the same `/user/balance`
en

dpoint as `x-dsh-auth-token`. No API key is needed, and the grant never
reaches the browser. When th

e account cannot answer (signed out, no account
provider in this composition, or the query failed) t

he API-key card stands in
and names its own route; a failed account query is reported on that fallba

ck
card, so "signed out" and "the query broke" stay distinguishable.

The account service's own balance query is deliberately **not** used: it goes to
`platform.deepseek.

com`, whose WAF answers non-browser clients with HTTP 429,
so it reports a failed balance instead of

e WAF answers non-browser clients with HTTP 429,
so it reports a failed balance instead of a number.

A failed or missing API-key read also reports the effective credential's
**source layer** and whethe

r this surface could write it
[该节后续省略]
## Security boundary

- API keys are used in the host half only and **never reach the browser**; the
browser reads same-or

igin JSON.
- `GET /dsh-plan-spend/snapshot` is a named route on the harness web server with
**no add

itional authentication**. When the web server binds `0.0.0.0`, anyone
on the same network can read t

he balance and quota numbers (never the keys).
Loopback-only use is unaffected.
